standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded elementary substructure
standard_prerequisites.statement: A$\leq$n B means that A is elementary in B already after adding any set of at most n elements of B.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation whose transitivity is asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Diamond condition
standard_prerequisites.statement: For unconfined A1, A2 and B containing A1 with A2 elementary in B, the intersection of A1 and A2 is elementary in A1.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the tool that splits the added set.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closure of unconfined systems
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unconfined systems are closed under the relevant operations, so the intermediate systems of the argument remain unconfined.
standard_prerequisites.use: It lets the diamond condition be applied.

core_obligations: Take a subset X of C outside A of size at most n and show that A is elementary in the union of A with X (source line 703).
Use that B is n-elementary in C to obtain that B is elementary in the union of B with X, and then apply the diamond condition to split the added elements between A and B (source line 703).
Use that A is n-elementary in B to obtain that A is elementary in the union of A with the part of X lying in B, and conclude the transitivity (source line 704).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to a set of at most n new elements and bring in the diamond condition.
Apply the boundedness hypothesis twice and conclude.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 701-702: the relation of bounded elementary substructure is transitive in the bound. The proof (source lines 703-705) is a short but genuinely structured argument: one takes a set of at most n elements outside A, writes it as the part lying in B together with the rest, obtains from the hypothesis on B and C that B is elementary in the enlarged B, splits the problem with the diamond condition, and then applies the hypothesis on A and B to the part lying in B. The statement records only the transitivity and neither the splitting of the added set nor the two applications of the boundedness hypothesis.
